name: multiple sclerosis overview
title: Multiple sclerosis: a relapse is new neurological dysfunction lasting 24 hours or more with no other cause; the typical relapses are myelitis, optic neuritis and brainstem or cerebellar syndromes; the diagnosis needs dissemination in space and time on MRI, with CSF oligoclonal bands able to stand in for time, once better explanations are ruled out (the VITAMIN differential, led by NMOSD and MOGAD); treatment is disease-modifying therapy by category plus symptomatic therapy

nodes.title: Could it be MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (MS)?
lines: an immune attack (B and T cells) on central nervous system myelin (oligodendrocytes) → axonal damage, then loss
most common disabling neurological disease of young adults in Canada (240 per 100,000) · women 3:1 · age 20-40 · white, Northern European
risk: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV, 32-fold: necessary, NOT sufficient) · genes explain 20-30% · adolescent obesity · smoking · diet · low vitamin D or sunlight · shift work
lesions: cortical or juxtacortical · periventricular · brainstem · cerebellum · spinal cord

nodes.title: A RELAPSE: which kind?
lines: NEW neurological symptoms · acute or subacute onset · lasting 24 HOURS or more · no other cause · not a pseudo-relapse
other features: sensory disturbances · fatigue · Lhermitte's sign (an electric shock down the back on bending the neck)

nodes.title: Myelitis
lines: spinal cord lesion · about 50% at onset

nodes.title: Optic neuritis
lines: about 25% at onset

nodes.title: Brainstem or cerebellar syndrome
lines: about 15% at onset

nodes.title: Below the lesion
lines: • sensory changes
• weakness
• bladder and bowel dysfunction

nodes.title: Vision
lines: • vision loss
• PAIN with eye movement

nodes.title: Eyes and balance
lines: • double vision · vertigo
• ataxia · slurred speech (dysarthria)
case: man in his 20s · vertigo, nausea, some double vision

nodes.title: MRI is central · lumbar puncture supports
lines: 2017 McDonald criteria: clinical attacks + MRI or CSF findings, combined

nodes.title: Disseminated in SPACE
lines: lesions in 2 or more typical regions:
• periventricular · cortical or juxtacortical
• infratentorial · spinal cord

nodes.title: Disseminated in TIME
lines: • a NEW lesion on follow-up MRI
• OR enhancing + non-enhancing lesions at once
• CSF oligoclonal bands can stand in for time

nodes.title: ALWAYS rule out a better explanation
lines: neuromyelitis optica (NMO) · myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein disease (MOGAD) · vascular · infection · metabolic (B12)

nodes.title: Differential: VITAMIN
lines: • V vascular: migraine, stroke, CADASIL
• I infection: HIV, syphilis, Lyme, West Nile
• T toxins: cocaine, additives
• A autoimmune: NMO, MOG · Sjögren's, Behçet's

nodes.title: VITAMIN, continued
lines: • M metabolic: B12
• I inflammatory: sarcoid
• N neoplastic: lymphoma

nodes.title: Top differential: how common
lines: • MS 1500 · NMOSD 30 · MOGAD 30
• sarcoid 15 · lymphoma 6
• ADEM 3 · Sjögren's 2

nodes.title: Course: clinically isolated syndrome → relapsing-remitting (85% at onset) → secondary progressive · or primary progressive from the start
lines: each labelled active or not, progressing or not · score disability on the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS, 0-10)
prognosis: 50% minor disability at 6-8 y · 21% need a walking aid at 15 y · median 27.9 y (age 59) to need one

nodes.title: Disease-modifying therapy: think in CATEGORIES
lines: • injectable platforms: interferons, glatiramer (Copaxone) · long-term safety data, LOW adherence
• standard orals: dimethyl fumarate, teriflunomide, fingolimod · easier than injections
• induction: cladribine · oral, effect lasts ~4 y
• high efficacy: natalizumab, B-cell therapies (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, rituximab) · B-cell therapies now very common

nodes.title: Treat the symptoms too
lines: • spasticity: baclofen, tizanidine, stretching, physiotherapy
• pain, tingling: amitriptyline, gabapentin, duloxetine, CBD
• bladder: solifenacin, urology referral · erections: sildenafil
• depression: antidepressants
• fatigue: amantadine, modafinil · walking: fampridine
